```json
{
  "edition_title": "Keen Africa Opportunities Digest: September 2026",
  "edition_intro": "The window on these opportunities is open right now, not someday. From a $10,000 energy innovation grant to a scholarship route into Germany's top graduate schools, every listing below is live, verifiable, and free to apply to. Move on the ones that fit your work before the deadlines below close.",
  "opportunities": [
    {
      "category": "scholarships",
      "title": "Heinrich Boll Foundation International Scholarship 2026/2027",
      "summary": "Fully funded Master's and PhD study in Germany for outstanding students from developing countries, including a monthly stipend and book allowance.",
      "deadline": "1 September 2026",
      "eligibility": "International students admitted to or applying for a Master's or PhD programme in Germany, priority to first-time applicants from DAC-list countries including Nigeria",
      "apply_url": "https://www.boell.de/en/applying-scholarship",
      "body_md": "The Heinrich Boll Foundation, affiliated with Germany's Green Party, funds graduate study for students who combine strong academics with civic or political engagement. Non-EU scholars receive a monthly stipend of 992 euros for Master's study (1,400 euros for doctoral study), a mobility allowance, health insurance support, and a 300 euro monthly book allowance for the full duration of the degree.\n\nThe application is entirely online and free: transcripts, a motivation letter connecting your academic plans to social or political engagement, and references. The Foundation places real weight on the engagement piece, so applicants who can point to concrete community or advocacy work stand out.\n\nFor Nigerians eyeing German universities, many of which charge no tuition even for international students, this scholarship removes the remaining cost barrier: living expenses. Applications for the Fall 2026 intake close 1 September 2026, with a second window opening 15 January 2027 for Spring intake."
    },
    {
      "category": "scholarships",
      "title": "AEIP Scholars Programme 2026/2027",
      "summary": "A fully sponsored Africa-Europe research collaboration pairing ten young scholars to co-develop solutions and present at international dialogues.",
      "deadline": "31 August 2026",
      "eligibility": "Researchers aged 25-35 enrolled in PhD, postdoc, or advanced study, based in Africa or Europe and affiliated with a recognised institution",
      "apply_url": "https://www.africaeuropeinnovation.net/scholars-programme/",
      "body_md": "The Africa-Europe Innovation Platform selects five African and five European scholars each cycle, pairs them into cross-continental teams, and funds them to produce a joint research output addressing a shared development challenge. It is a rare structure: rather than competing for a single prize, you are matched with a European counterpart and resourced to build something together.\n\nThe application starts with an Expression of Interest built around a short abstract of your proposed research direction. Selection favours scholars whose work has a clear path to real-world application, not just academic novelty.\n\nWinning pairs are sponsored to present at the AEIP Stakeholder Meeting in Europe in June 2027, and the top three pairs are invited to the Africa-Europe Innovation Dialogues 2027, a platform that puts early-career researchers in front of policymakers and funders who rarely take unsolicited meetings."
    },
    {
      "category": "scholarships",
      "title": "Gates Cambridge Scholarship 2027",
      "summary": "Full-ride funding to pursue any postgraduate course at the University of Cambridge, covering tuition, living costs, and travel.",
      "deadline": "6 January 2027",
      "eligibility": "Nigerian citizens applying for a Master's or PhD at Cambridge for 2027/28 entry; must apply through the Cambridge course application and opt in for Gates funding",
      "apply_url": "https://www.gatescambridge.org/apply/",
      "body_md": "Gates Cambridge is one of the most competitive postgraduate scholarships in the world, and it is explicitly open to Nigerian applicants alongside a short list of other African countries. It funds any subject at any level, from a one-year Master's to a PhD, at one of the world's oldest and best-resourced universities.\n\nThere is no separate scholarship application: you apply for your Cambridge course through the standard university portal and tick the box indicating you want to be considered for Gates funding within that same process. The University's application portal for 2027 entry reopens in September 2026, with course deadlines falling between 8 December 2026 and 6 January 2027 depending on subject.\n\nThe scholarship covers the full cost of studying at Cambridge: tuition, a maintenance allowance, and one return flight per year. Given Cambridge's academic reputation, this is one of the highest-leverage scholarships a Nigerian student can put on a CV, and the lead time between now and the January deadline is enough to build a genuinely strong application rather than rush one."
    },
    {
      "category": "grants",
      "title": "Social Shifters Global Innovation Challenge 2026",
      "summary": "Up to $15,000 in grant funding for young founders already running a social-impact venture, with no equity taken.",
      "deadline": "31 August 2026",
      "eligibility": "Founders aged 18-30 with decision-making authority over a startup or project already delivering measurable social or environmental impact",
      "apply_url": "https://www.socialshifters.co/global-innovation-challenge/",
      "body_md": "Social Shifters runs this challenge specifically for young people who have moved past the idea stage: your project needs to already be operating and producing measurable outputs tied to at least one UN Sustainable Development Goal. That bar filters out idea-stage applicants, which means less competition for founders who are actually building.\n\nMultiple awards of up to $15,000 are available, alongside connection to a global community of young impact leaders and exposure through Social Shifters' partner brands. The application runs through the organisation's own awards platform and is free to enter.\n\nFor a Nigerian founder running an early but proven venture, whether in agritech, education, health, or climate, this is real non-dilutive capital with a fast, straightforward process and a deadline that gives you time to prepare a tight submission."
    },
    {
      "category": "grants",
      "title": "USAID Development Innovation Ventures (DIV) Fund",
      "summary": "Rolling grants from $25,000 up to $5 million for evidence-backed, cost-effective innovations tackling development challenges in USAID-supported countries.",
      "deadline": "Rolling",
      "eligibility": "Individuals, nonprofits, and for-profit organisations with a project operating in a USAID-supported country, including Nigeria",
      "apply_url": "https://www.div.fund/apply",
      "body_value": "",
      "body_md": "DIV is one of the largest open-application funding mechanisms available to African innovators, structured in three stages so the amount of funding grows as your evidence base grows. Stage 1 offers $25,000 to $200,000 to test a new idea, Stage 2 offers $200,000 to $1.5 million to rigorously evaluate what is working, and Stage 3 offers up to $5 million to scale something that has already proven itself.\n\nApplications are accepted on a rolling basis with no submission deadline, which means there is no reason to wait for a cohort to open. The application asks for a clear articulation of the problem, why your approach is more cost-effective than existing alternatives, and what evidence would prove it works.\n\nBecause DIV funds individuals and for-profits as well as nonprofits, it is open to Nigerian entrepreneurs building for-profit ventures with a genuine development angle, not just NGOs. The rolling structure rewards founders who apply as soon as they have something worth testing rather than waiting for a deadline that does not exist."
    },
    {
      "category": "conferences",
      "title": "One Young World Leading Scholarship 2026",
      "summary": "Fully funded delegate place at the One Young World Summit 2026 in Cape Town, covering flights, hotel, and meals for four days.",
      "deadline": "31 October 2026",
      "eligibility": "Young leaders aged 18-35 with a demonstrated record of impact, priority given to first-time Summit attendees from under-represented countries",
      "apply_url": "https://www.oneyoungworld.com/scholarship/leading-scholarship-2026",
      "body_md": "One Young World is the closest thing the youth leadership world has to a global mainstage: 2,200 delegates from 190-plus countries, and a lifelong Ambassador network of over 20,000 alumni that includes people who go on to run companies, NGOs, and government initiatives. The 2026 Summit takes place in Cape Town from 3 to 6 November, which puts it within easy reach of Nigerian delegates in terms of both cost and time zone.\n\nThe Leading Scholarship covers round-trip travel, hotel accommodation for the full Summit, and all meals, so the only real cost to a successful applicant is time. Selection prioritises candidates who can point to specific, verifiable impact in their community or field, not just potential.\n\nBeyond the four days on stage, delegates get access to the Action Accelerator programme, mentorship from global leaders, and in many cases the opening to represent Nigeria during the Summit's Opening Ceremony. It is one of the few free routes onto a genuinely international stage before the age of 35."
    },
    {
      "category": "competitions",
      "title": "ECOWAS Startup Awards 2026",
      "summary": "A regional pitch competition offering $65,000 in cash prizes to the top three West African startups, with no equity taken.",
      "deadline": "31 August 2026",
      "eligibility": "Startups based in an ECOWAS member state, founded or led by citizens of ECOWAS countries, operating in EdTech, FinTech, HealthTech, AgriTech, CleanTech, or Tourism",
      "apply_url": "https://ecowasstartupawards.ipawas.org/",
      "body_value": "",
      "body_md": "This is the first edition of a genuinely regional prize built to spotlight West African startups beyond the usual Lagos-Nairobi-Cape Town circuit. The top winner takes $30,000, with $20,000 and $15,000 going to the two runners-up, and none of it comes with an equity string attached.\n\nBeyond the cash, winners get a six-month acceleration and mentorship programme, regional visibility across ECOWAS member states, and direct access to investor deal rooms, the kind of introductions that are usually gatekept behind expensive accelerator programmes.\n\nTo apply you need at least two years of operating history, a working product with evidence of traction, and the standard documentation: registration certificate, financials, business plan, pitch deck, and a one-minute video pitch. For Nigerian startups with real traction in one of the six priority sectors, this is a low-friction shot at serious non-dilutive capital before the month is out."
    },
    {
      "category": "competitions",
      "title": "Africa Energy Innovation Challenge (AEIC) 2026",
      "summary": "A pan-African pitch competition offering up to $10,000 in grant prizes plus mentorship for youth-led energy and sustainability solutions.",
      "deadline": "10 September 2026",
      "eligibility": "Teams of at least three people aged 18-35, including at least one woman and one man, proposing solutions to energy access, agribusiness, fintech, AI, or connectivity challenges",
      "apply_url": "https://thenef.org/aeic/",
      "body_md": "Now in its 11th edition, AEIC is organised by the Nigeria Energy Forum and has built a track record of pushing early-stage teams straight into rooms with investors and industry decision-makers. This year's theme, accelerating value addition, youth innovation, and community action, reflects a deliberate push toward practical, deployable ideas over pure concept pitches.\n\nWinning teams share cash prizes of up to $10,000, and finalists, even those who do not win, get business development mentorship and incubator support valued at over $15,000. Twenty or more shortlisted teams also receive complimentary passes to the 11th Nigeria Energy Forum in November, a networking opportunity that alone is worth the application effort.\n\nThe team-composition requirement, at least one woman and one man per team, is unusual and worth planning around early if you are assembling a group. Submissions are proposals at this stage; shortlisted teams pitch prototype models virtually ahead of the November forum."
    },
    {
      "category": "certifications",
      "title": "3MTT DeepTech_Ready Upskilling Programme",
      "summary": "A free, government-backed six-month training track in AI, data science, and deep tech, with certification and internship pathways.",
      "deadline": "Rolling",
      "eligibility": "Nigerian citizens, including 3MTT Fellows and individuals with basic to intermediate technical knowledge",
      "apply_url": "https://3mtt.nitda.gov.ng/deeptech/",
      "body_md": "3MTT (3 Million Technical Talent) is the Nigerian Federal Government's flagship digital skills initiative, run through the Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy and NITDA. The DeepTech_Ready track sits above the general 3MTT cohorts, focused specifically on Data Science, AI, and other advanced technical fields, built in partnership with Data Science Nigeria and supported by Google.org.\n\nThere is no application fee, no IELTS requirement, and no fixed closing date, applications are accepted continuously as new cohorts form. Each cohort runs for six months of structured technical and professional development, ending in certification.\n\nThe programme has already trained over 135,000 fellows directly since its 2023 launch, and in 2026 it opened a Talent Registry connecting graduates to more than 3,000 active tech job listings. For a Nigerian who wants advanced AI or data science skills without paying for a bootcamp, this is the most direct government-backed route available."
    },
    {
      "category": "certifications",
      "title": "IBM SkillsBuild Free Courses and Certificates",
      "summary": "Unlimited free access to IBM's course catalogue in AI, cybersecurity, data, and cloud, with digital certificates on completion.",
      "deadline": "Rolling",
      "eligibility": "Open to all learners globally, including students, recent graduates, and career changers in Nigeria",
      "apply_url": "https://skillsbuild.org/",
      "body_md": "IBM SkillsBuild is a permanent, always-open learning platform rather than a time-boxed cohort programme, which makes it one of the lowest-friction ways to build a credible technical certificate portfolio. The catalogue spans AI, cybersecurity, data analysis, and cloud computing, structured in self-paced modules with assessments and completion certificates.\n\nThere is no application process beyond creating a free account: no waitlist, no selection committee, no deadline pressure. That also means it rewards self-discipline rather than a one-time application effort, the value comes from consistently working through the material.\n\nIBM has also run region-specific expansions of the programme across Africa, including partnerships supporting tens of thousands of learners in East and Southern Africa, but the core global platform at skillsbuild.org is open to any Nigerian learner today, with no geographic restriction on enrolment."
    },
    {
      "category": "certifications",
      "title": "TechUp Africa TAMP DataCamp Tech Skills Scholarship 2026",
      "summary": "Free premium access to over 450 DataCamp courses in data science, AI, Python, and SQL for young Africans, delivered through DataCamp Donates.",
      "deadline": "30 August 2026",
      "eligibility": "Young Africans, students, recent graduates, and career changers able to commit to active learning for three to six months",
      "apply_url": "https://techupafrica.org/",
      "body_md": "TechUp Africa partners with DataCamp Donates to distribute premium DataCamp licenses, normally a paid subscription, to young Africans at no cost. The scholarship unlocks the full course catalogue: Python, SQL, Power BI, machine learning, and applied data science, along with practice exercises, skill assessments, and DataCamp's Certification and Workspace features.\n\nThe application itself is a short form covering your background and current situation, with no fee at any stage. The one condition worth noting: TechUp Africa can revoke the license if it sits unused for two consecutive months, so this is best suited to applicants who are ready to start immediately rather than banking the credential for later.\n\nFor a Nigerian building toward a data or AI career, a DataCamp license normally costs real money every month, this scholarship removes that cost entirely for the duration of active study, provided you actually put in the hours."
    },
    {
      "category": "certifications",
      "title": "Google Career Certificates via Coursera Financial Aid",
      "summary": "Fully sponsored access to Google's job-ready certificates in IT Support, Data Analytics, Cybersecurity, UX Design, and Project Management.",
      "deadline": "Rolling",
      "eligibility": "Any learner globally who demonstrates financial need, including Nigerian applicants",
      "apply_url": "https://grow.google/certificates/",
      "body_md": "Google Career Certificates are designed to make someone job-ready in three to six months without a prior degree, covering some of the most in-demand entry points into tech: IT Support, Data Analytics, Cybersecurity, UX Design, Digital Marketing, and Project Management. Normally hosted on Coursera at roughly $39 a month, the certificates become free for learners who qualify for financial aid.\n\nThe application is built into the Coursera enrolment flow: on any Google Career Certificate course page, click Financial Aid Available next to the Enroll button and complete a short form explaining your financial situation and career goals. There is no separate deadline or cohort structure, it runs continuously.\n\nGoogle also distributes certificate scholarships through partner organisations active in Nigeria, so learners who do not qualify directly through Coursera's financial aid form have a second route through local NGO and community partners. Either way, the certificates themselves carry real weight with employers who already recognise the Google name."
    }
  ]
}
```
